v.rationale:
All three suites pass (19, 15 and 23 tests). All three correctly keep the row and exit 1 when a real local-disk permission failure occurs (checked by probe with a chmod 0555 directory).

**impl-1 (rank 1)** is the only one that fully meets "carry on with the rest". It catches and reports any Throwable from the disk, so the run continues and still exits 1. It uses lazyById with a narrow select, and its explicit shared cache lock blocks real purges while leaving dry-runs free. Its tests are the most complete on failure paths, including a genuine retry on the next run. Its one weakness is a delete query per row.

**impl-3 (rank 2)** has the most idiomatic modern code: Isolatable, fail(), partition, and a batched delete per chunk. But the isolation mutex covers dry-run and the confirmation prompt, so a preview during the nightly run fails and a prompt left open blocks the 03:00 run. An unexpected exception from the disk aborts the whole run. Its tests include a no-op "retry" test and an anonymous subclass that re-declares the command signature.

**impl-2 (rank 3)** is clean and simple, with a correct lock and batched deletes. It shares the unguarded-delete abort and puts a side effect inside filter(). Its tests are thinner on production confirmation: there is no interactive yes/no case and the refusal test checks no output.
